Why is Lord Shiva's throat blue?

When the devas and asuras churned the Ocean of Milk for amrit, the first thing to rise was Halahala, a poison so deadly it began to burn all the worlds. Everyone ran to Lord Shiva.

Out of compassion for all beings, Shiva took the poison in his palm and drank it. He held it in his throat, and it turned blue. That is why he is called Neelkantha, the blue-throated one.

The lesson: great souls take on pain so that others may be safe.

Source: Bhagavata Purana, Canto 8, Chapter 7; Mahabharata, Adi Parva 18.
